column1: # mrk macOS defaults: the keys to skip
# The keys of config/defaults.tsv that defaults.sh (make defaults) does not
# write. A key stays in config/defaults.tsv, with its description, so MRK-1
# still shows it, and so it can come back. defaults.sh --check calls such a
# key skipped, and Dipstick's mrk Settings shows it as off.
# defaults.sh --skip DOMAIN KEY adds a line, and --unskip DOMAIN KEY deletes
# one. Neither changes the Mac: --revert DOMAIN KEY puts back the value the
# key had before mrk wrote it, and --key DOMAIN KEY writes mrk's value.
# One key on each line: the domain and the key, as config/defaults.tsv has
# them, separated by a tab, with the same escapes. A line that starts with #
# is a comment, and an empty line is ignored. Keep the lines in byte order
# (LC_ALL=C sort): --skip adds a line before the first line that sorts after
# it, and --unskip deletes a line by its exact text. defaults.sh refuses the
# file, before it writes anything, when a line is not one key of
# config/defaults.tsv or when two lines name one key.
